description: How a warehouse's semantic models become names an agent can call. Every source's models feed one registry of members: each model's dimensions and metrics, and the facts labelled as filters. A member answers to its bare name, to `parent.name`, and to either qualified by its model as `MODEL::name` or `MODEL::parent.name`; the last of these is its key. Errors are pinned as a kind and the names the message must mention, since the wording belongs to each language.

models.description: The models every case below reads, all on the source `warehouse`, with the governed data-dict definitions on the same source. Members not given a parent belong to no logical table. `parameters` are a model's typed parameters, and `stubs` are models listed on the same source but not yet read.

registry.description: The members the registry lists for those models, in order: per model, its dimensions, then its metrics, then the facts labelled as filters. Named filters and other facts are context only and are not listed. `synonyms` is the member's synonyms joined by spaces.

resolution.description: Resolving names against the registry as one kind of member. `filter` resolves only the members labelled as filters. Braces around a name, as the SQL token syntax writes it, are ignored. `expected` is the keys resolved, in order, or an error: `ambiguous` when more than one member of the kind answers to the name, `wrong_kind` when members answer to it but none of the kind, and `missing` when none does.

metric_origin.description: Which pool a metric name belongs to when data-dict metric definitions and native semantic metrics share a source. A definition answers to `name` or `table::name`. A name both pools answer to is ambiguous, and must be qualified.

pool_text.description: What search_pool returns when the pool holds only these models, the stubs beside them, and no measures or definitions. Members and stubs are ranked with the pool's lexical ranking: a member by its name, model, kind, label, description, and synonyms, and a stub by its name, label, backend, and description. A member is written by its bare name when that is unambiguous and by its key otherwise. `source_names` are the sources an agent with several names; a member on one of them says so. `empty` is the reply for a pool with nothing in it.

call_metrics.description: Calls over native metrics that are refused before any SQL runs, on the source holding these models and definitions. A call draws its metrics from data-dict definitions or from one native semantic model, never both and never two models, resolves its dimensions within that model, and binds `arguments` only to that model's declared parameters. `arguments` is the JSON text the model writes. Each pinned phrase must appear in the error.

cases.name: metrics from both pools in one call are refused

mentions: Metrics in one call must come from either data-dict definitions or one native semantic model.

cases.name: native metrics from two models in one call are refused

mentions: Metrics in one call must belong to one native semantic model.

cases.name: arguments are refused for data-dict metrics

mentions: `arguments` is supported only for native semantic metrics.
